text: Figure 7.3: ClientServerInterface. Server side Basically Dds consumes the application PDU and, according to the internal logic, can decide to produce and transmit a new RTPS PDU through the transport layer. The DataWriter and DataReader represent internal functional blocks showing the mapping between a PDU and the related DDS middleware object (they are modeled in the ECUC by some DdsDataWriter/DdsDataReader). The RTPS processor represents the logic of module. Considering the transmission direction, the application data is fed into the Dds T ransformer, which simply copies the VariableDataPrototype and ClientServerOperation into a buffer that will serve as the content of the DdsRtpsDataTxPdu. In the reverse direction, the VariableDataPrototype and ClientServerOperation results are similarly extracted from the received PDU. The TriggerInterface use case can be considered as a special case of the SenderReceiverInterface where the data is empty , so in this case the Dds T ransformer is not used.
